newsitem.title: UK: Dirty tankers steady, Med Aframaxes seen firming.
newsitem.headline: Dirty tankers steady, Med Aframaxes seen firming.

text.p: The dirty tanker market was generally quiet but stable on Monday, with some brokers expecting cross-Mediterranean rates to firm on 80,000-tonne cargoes.

Middle East very large crude carriers (VLCCs) remained at their year high of W75 on eastward voyages, or slightly higher for modern ships to Japan. Voyages to U.K./Cont, meanwhile, continued to be pegged at W60.
Two brokers said they expected cross-Med Aframax (80,000 tonners) to rise after good activity last week.
"There were quite a few fixtures but rates stayed at W110. This week if activity remains good, they could go up to W115," one broker said.
"Nothing much has been done in the Med today but there are cargoes around. I think Aframax rates are going to rise," another said.
But he was less optimistic about rates for 130,000 tonne vessels (Suezmaxes) which have been languishing at W95 for some time and predicted that these "could fall if things do not get any livelier."
Meanwhile, the West Africa market was steady with VLCCs remaining at W65 and Suezmaxes at around W87.5.
In the transatlantic market, the 300,000 tonne Arcadia was heard done at W65 for Koch and the 280,000 tonne Megara at W67.5 for Irving.

Inter-U.K./Cont Aframaxes were steady to slightly firmer at W95, and some brokers said this sector could edge up in line with the cross-Med market and on tightness of tonnage. Fuel oil was steady at W245 for 25,000 tonnes inter-U.K./Cont and slightly firmer in the Med at W200.
The Caribs/upcoast market was flat with 70,000 tonne crude and 50,000 tonne fuel cargoes both at W200. --London newsroom +44 171 542 4088
